whyWrongByChoice.E: Negative selection is a central tolerance mechanism; peripheral tolerance uses deletion, anergy, and Treg inhibition.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A patient with an established autoimmune disease initially had antibodies to a single self-protein, but over years develops reactivity to several additional self-antigens as tissue damage releases previously hidden self-proteins. Which phenomenon best describes this expansion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bystander activation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Central tolerance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Epitope spreading

choices.label: D
choices.text: Molecular mimicry

choices.label: E
choices.text: Negative selection

explanation.summary: Epitope spreading is the amplification of autoimmunity as the response expands to additional self-epitopes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines epitope spreading as expansion of the immune response beyond its initial target to recognize additional epitopes within the same or different molecules, made accessible by proteolysis, oxidative modification, or structural changes in damaged tissue. It cites evidence in multiple sclerosis, SLE, type 1 diabetes, and pemphigus vulgaris.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Bystander activation refers to CTL-mediated killing of nearby uninfected cells during infection, not expanding antigen recognition over time.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Central tolerance is a protective deletion process, not a mechanism of disease expansion.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Molecular mimicry describes cross-reactivity between microbial and self-antigens that share homology, not progressive broadening to new self-epitopes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Negative selection removes autoreactive developing lymphocytes and does not broaden an autoimmune response.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man has several months of low back pain and morning stiffness that improve with exercise; imaging shows sacroiliitis. He previously had an episode of reactive arthritis. Which HLA subtype is most associated with his condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: HLA-DQ2

choices.label: B
choices.text: HLA-DR2

choices.label: C
choices.text: HLA-DR4

choices.label: D
choices.text: HLA-DQ8

choices.label: E
choices.text: HLA-B27

explanation.summary: HLA-B27 is linked to ankylosing spondylitis and the other seronegative spondyloarthropathies.
explanation.whyCorrect: Table 1 associates HLA-B27 with psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, IBD-associated arthritis, and reactive arthritis. Inflammatory back pain with sacroiliitis that improves with exercise, plus prior reactive arthritis, fits the B27-associated spondyloarthropathy spectrum.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HLA-DQ2 is associated with celiac disease.
whyWrongByChoice.B: HLA-DR2 is associated with multiple sclerosis, SLE, and Goodpasture syndrome.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HLA-DR4 is associated with rheumatoid arthritis, type 1 diabetes, and Addison disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HLA-DQ8 is associated with celiac disease, not spondyloarthropathy.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: An epidemiologist notes that most autoimmune diseases are more common in women, especially those of child-bearing age. According to the brick, which postulated mechanism best explains this sex difference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Estrogen enhances negative selection in the thymus

choices.label: B
choices.text: Estrogen may reduce apoptosis of autoreactive lymphocytes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Estrogen upregulates MHC class I on nucleated cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pregnancy permanently deletes all regulatory T cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: Testosterone directly stimulates autoantibody production

explanation.summary: The brick attributes the female predominance of autoimmune disease to estrogen limiting apoptosis of autoreactive lymphocytes.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists sex and age as intrinsic risk factors, noting most known autoimmune diseases are more common in women, particularly women of child-bearing age, and that the postulated mechanism is that high levels of estrogen may reduce apoptosis of autoreactive lymphocytes, allowing them to persist.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The brick proposes estrogen reduces apoptosis of autoreactive cells; it does not enhance negative selection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Estrogen-driven MHC class I upregulation is not the mechanism the brick proposes for female predominance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Permanent deletion of all Tregs by pregnancy is not a mechanism described in the brick.
whyWrongByChoice.E: The brick attributes risk to estrogen effects, not testosterone-driven autoantibody production.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A second-year medical student is asked to contrast autoinflammatory diseases with autoimmune diseases. Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the two categories?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoinflammatory diseases are common, whereas autoimmune diseases are rare

choices.label: B
choices.text: Autoinflammatory diseases are driven primarily by genetic factors, whereas autoimmune diseases are typically multifactorial

choices.label: C
choices.text: Autoinflammatory diseases are mediated by T and B lymphocytes, whereas autoimmune diseases are mediated by neutrophils and macrophages

choices.label: D
choices.text: Autoinflammatory diseases involve a breakdown in immune tolerance, whereas autoimmune diseases do not

choices.label: E
choices.text: Autoinflammatory diseases produce autoantibodies, whereas autoimmune diseases produce inflammatory cytokines only

explanation.summary: Autoinflammatory conditions are driven primarily by genetic factors such as loss-of-function mutations in inflammasome inhibitors, whereas autoimmune diseases are complex and multifactorial.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick summary states that autoinflammatory conditions are driven primarily by genetic factors, such as loss-of-function mutations in inhibitors of the inflammasome, and that few autoimmune disorders are monogenic; the development of autoimmune diseases is instead complex and multifactorial, influenced by intrinsic factors, environmental factors, and amplification loops.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Autoinflammatory diseases are rare, whereas up to 10% of people develop an autoimmune disease during their lifetime.
whyWrongByChoice.C: This is reversed: autoinflammatory tissue damage is caused by neutrophils and macrophages (innate cells), while autoimmune damage is mediated by T and B cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: This is reversed: autoimmune diseases involve a breakdown in immune tolerance, while autoinflammatory diseases do not directly involve the breakdown of tolerance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Autoantibodies define autoimmunity, not autoinflammation; autoinflammatory disease reflects inappropriate secretion of inflammatory cytokines or granule contents by innate cells.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A public health researcher is preparing a lecture on the burden of autoimmune disease. Approximately what proportion of people develop an autoimmune disease at some point in their lives?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Less than 1%

choices.label: B
choices.text: Up to 10%

choices.label: C
choices.text: About 25%

choices.label: D
choices.text: About 50%

choices.label: E
choices.text: More than 75%

explanation.summary: Up to 10% of people develop an autoimmune disease at some point in their life.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that in autoimmunity, lymphocytes or antibodies mistakenly recognize self-antigen as non-self and initiate an adaptive immune response, and that up to 10% of people develop an autoimmune disease at some point in their life. This contrasts with autoinflammatory diseases, which are described as rare.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Less than 1% underestimates the burden; the brick cites a figure of up to 10%.
whyWrongByChoice.C: About 25% overstates the lifetime frequency given in the brick.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Half of the population is far higher than the stated figure of up to 10%.
whyWrongByChoice.E: More than three-quarters of people do not develop autoimmune disease; the brick cites up to 10%.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A 12-year-old boy with a monogenic periodic fever syndrome undergoes biopsy of an acutely inflamed joint during an attack. Serum testing shows no autoantibodies. Tissue damage in his condition is caused primarily by which of the following cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: CD4+ and CD8+ effector T cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Follicular dendritic cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mast cells and tissue eosinophils

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neutrophils and macrophages

choices.label: E
choices.text: Plasma cells and their antibodies

explanation.summary: Autoinflammatory diseases produce inflammation and tissue damage caused by neutrophils and macrophages of the innate immune system.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick defines autoinflammation as innate immune system malfunction with inappropriate secretion of inflammatory cytokines or granule contents, and states that autoinflammatory diseases are the result of inflammation and tissue damage caused by neutrophils and macrophages. A monogenic periodic fever syndrome without autoantibodies is an autoinflammatory disorder.

whyWrongByChoice.A: T-cell-mediated damage characterizes autoimmune disease, in which the adaptive immune system is dysregulated.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Follicular dendritic cells present immune complexes to B cells during affinity maturation and are not the source of autoinflammatory damage.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Mast cells and eosinophils are not the effector cells the brick identifies for autoinflammatory tissue damage.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Plasma cells produce antibodies, including autoantibodies in autoimmune disease; this patient has no autoantibodies.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: An immature B cell in the bone marrow binds a self-antigen with high avidity. Rather than being deleted, the cell changes its antigen receptor so that the new receptor no longer recognizes the self-antigen, and the cell continues development. Which of the following tolerance processes does this represent?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Affinity maturation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Anergy

choices.label: C
choices.text: Receptor editing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Somatic hypermutation

choices.label: E
choices.text: Suppression by regulatory T cells

explanation.summary: Receptor editing is a central tolerance outcome for self-reactive B cells in the bone marrow, alongside deletion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Figure 2 of the brick shows that central tolerance for B cells occurs in the bone marrow, where a self-reactive B cell undergoes either deletion or receptor editing. Receptor editing replaces the self-reactive receptor so that the cell is no longer autoreactive, which is exactly the scenario described.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Affinity maturation increases antibody affinity during an ongoing response; it is not a mechanism for eliminating self-reactivity in developing B cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Anergy (failure to respond) is a peripheral tolerance mechanism acting on circulating lymphocytes; it does not change the receptor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Somatic hypermutation refines the affinity of an existing antibody response over time and is described by the brick in the context of epitope spreading, not developing B cells in the marrow.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Regulatory T-cell suppression is a peripheral tolerance mechanism acting on circulating T and B cells, not a bone marrow developmental step.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: An infant is found to have a thymic defect that abolishes one of the two components of central tolerance. Negative selection is intact, yet self-reactive T and B cells that reach the periphery are not suppressed. Which of the following processes is most likely defective?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deletion of circulating lymphocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Expression of MHC class I on nucleated cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Generation of regulatory T cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Induction of anergy

choices.label: E
choices.text: Receptor editing of B cells

explanation.summary: Central tolerance consists of negative selection and the generation of regulatory T cells in the thymus, which then suppress self-reactive lymphocytes in the periphery.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that central tolerance consists of deleting self-reactive lymphocytes (negative selection) and the generation of regulatory T cells. Figure 2 shows regulatory T cells developing in the thymus and then migrating to the periphery to suppress self-reactive T and B cells. If negative selection is intact but peripheral suppression is absent, the thymic generation of regulatory T cells is the defective component.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Deletion of circulating lymphocytes is a peripheral tolerance mechanism; the stem describes a thymic (central) defect.
whyWrongByChoice.B: MHC class I expression enables cytotoxic T-cell recognition of abnormal cells and is not a component of central tolerance.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anergy is a peripheral tolerance mechanism, not one of the two components of central tolerance.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Receptor editing occurs in the bone marrow for B cells, not in the thymus.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A mature, circulating T cell encounters an antigen-presenting cell displaying a self-antigen. Afterward the T cell survives but fails to respond to that antigen on subsequent encounters. Which of the following peripheral tolerance mechanisms does this describe?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anergy

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deletion

choices.label: C
choices.text: Epitope spreading

choices.label: D
choices.text: Negative selection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Receptor editing

explanation.summary: Anergy is the induction of non-responsiveness in a circulating self-reactive lymphocyte that remains alive.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick lists peripheral tolerance mechanisms as deletion of self-reactive lymphocytes, induction of anergy (non-responsiveness), or inhibition by regulatory T cells. Figure 2 labels anergy as a failure to respond following encounter with an APC presenting self antigen. A surviving but unresponsive T cell is anergic.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Deletion kills the self-reactive cell; here the cell survives.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Epitope spreading is an amplification mechanism of autoimmunity, not a tolerance mechanism.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Negative selection is a central tolerance process that deletes developing lymphocytes in the thymus or bone marrow, not mature circulating cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Receptor editing is a bone marrow process for developing B cells, not a peripheral T-cell mechanism.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A macrophage's toll-like receptors bind conserved structures on an invading bacterium. One specific effect of this stimulation is activation of a multiprotein complex. Activation and secretion of which of the following cytokines is the direct product of that complex?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IFN-gamma

choices.label: B
choices.text: IL-1

choices.label: C
choices.text: IL-2

choices.label: D
choices.text: IL-6

choices.label: E
choices.text: TNF-alpha

explanation.summary: The inflammasome is a multiprotein complex activated downstream of PRR stimulation that induces the activation and secretion of IL-1.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick explains that PRRs such as toll-like receptors recognize PAMPs and DAMPs, and that one specific effect of PRR stimulation is activation of the inflammasome, a multiprotein complex capable of inducing the activation and secretion of IL-1. This is why pyrin loss-of-function (loss of inflammasome suppression) leads to IL-1 overexpression.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IFN-gamma is a T-cell cytokine the brick mentions in amplifying dendritic cell activation, not an inflammasome product.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IL-2 is not among the cytokines the brick associates with PRR signaling or the inflammasome.
whyWrongByChoice.D: IL-6 is one of the three major pro-inflammatory cytokines produced after PRR binding, but the brick ties inflammasome activity specifically to IL-1.
whyWrongByChoice.E: TNF-alpha is also a major pro-inflammatory cytokine downstream of PRR signaling, but it is not the cytokine the inflammasome activates.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: Binding of pathogen-associated molecular patterns to pattern-recognition receptors on innate immune cells initiates NF-kB and IRF signaling and results in secretion of three major pro-inflammatory cytokines. Which of the following sets lists those cytokines?

choices.label: A
choices.text: IFN-gamma, IL-12, and IL-18

choices.label: B
choices.text: IL-1, IL-6, and TNF-alpha

choices.label: C
choices.text: IL-10, TGF-beta, and IL-35

choices.label: D
choices.text: IL-2, IL-4, and IL-5

choices.label: E
choices.text: IL-4, IL-13, and IL-9

explanation.summary: IL-1, IL-6, and TNF-alpha are the three major pro-inflammatory cytokines produced as a result of PRR binding.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that PRR binding initiates NF-kB and IRF signaling, inducing changes in cytokine secretion, adhesion molecule expression, and costimulatory molecule expression, and that IL-1, IL-6, and TNF-alpha are the three major pro-inflammatory cytokines produced as a result of PRR binding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IFN-gamma appears in the brick only as a T-cell cytokine that amplifies dendritic cell activation; this set is not the PRR-driven trio.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IL-10, TGF-beta, and IL-35 are not the trio the brick names as products of PRR stimulation.
whyWrongByChoice.D: IL-2, IL-4, and IL-5 are not the pro-inflammatory cytokines the brick attributes to PRR binding.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IL-4, IL-13, and IL-9 are not the cytokines the brick identifies as the major products of innate PRR signaling.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A 48-year-old woman has 6 months of symmetric swelling of the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints of both hands with prolonged morning stiffness. Serum rheumatoid factor is positive. The autoantibody detected in her serum is associated with which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A type 1 hypersensitivity reaction mediated by IgE

choices.label: B
choices.text: A type 2 hypersensitivity reaction causing cellular dysfunction

choices.label: C
choices.text: A type 3 hypersensitivity reaction causing systemic inflammation

choices.label: D
choices.text: A type 4 hypersensitivity reaction mediated by T cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: An autoinflammatory reaction driven by IL-1 overexpression

explanation.summary: Rheumatoid factor is associated with rheumatoid arthritis, a type 3 hypersensitivity reaction causing systemic inflammation.
explanation.whyCorrect: In the Mechanisms of Damage section, the brick states that the target of autoreactivity is tightly associated with the systems affected, and that rheumatoid factor is associated with rheumatoid arthritis, a type 3 HSR causing systemic inflammation. Symmetric small-joint polyarthritis with a positive rheumatoid factor fits this description.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Type 1 IgE-mediated hypersensitivity is not among the mechanisms of autoimmune damage; the brick lists types 2, 3, and 4.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Type 2 HSR with cellular dysfunction describes anti-AChR antibody in myasthenia gravis, not rheumatoid factor.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Type 4 HSR is T-cell mediated, as in celiac disease; rheumatoid factor is an antibody-associated type 3 process.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IL-1-driven autoinflammatory disease does not involve autoantibodies such as rheumatoid factor.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man with newly diagnosed Crohn's disease undergoes genetic testing and is found to carry two mutated NOD2 alleles. Compared with individuals who do not carry these mutations, his risk of developing Crohn's disease was increased by approximately which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 2- to 3-fold

choices.label: B
choices.text: 5- to 10-fold

choices.label: C
choices.text: 20- to 40-fold

choices.label: D
choices.text: 100-fold

choices.label: E
choices.text: 1000-fold

explanation.summary: Carrying two mutated NOD2 alleles increases the risk of Crohn's disease 20- to 40-fold.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's clinical correlation states that the strongest risk factor for Crohn's disease is a mutation in NOD2, a PRR that recognizes microbial components, and that individuals who carry two of these mutated NOD2 alleles have a 20- to 40-fold increased risk of developing Crohn's disease. The mutations are postulated to cause inappropriate NF-kB activation in monocytes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A 2- to 3-fold increase underestimates the effect; a 3- to 4-fold increase is the figure the brick gives for smoking, not for NOD2 homozygosity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: A 5- to 10-fold increase is lower than the 20- to 40-fold risk stated for two mutated alleles.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A 100-fold increase overstates the risk the brick cites.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A 1000-fold increase far exceeds the 20- to 40-fold figure.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman who smokes one pack of cigarettes daily is diagnosed with Crohn's disease. She asks how her smoking relates to her illness. Which of the following is the most accurate response?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Smoking does not change the risk but makes ileal involvement more likely than colonic

choices.label: B
choices.text: Smoking lowers the risk 3-4 times and makes colonic involvement more likely than ileal

choices.label: C
choices.text: Smoking raises the risk 20-40 times and makes colonic involvement more likely than ileal

choices.label: D
choices.text: Smoking raises the risk 3-4 times and makes colonic involvement more likely than ileal

choices.label: E
choices.text: Smoking raises the risk 3-4 times and makes ileal involvement more likely than colonic

explanation.summary: Smoking is a modifiable risk factor that increases Crohn's disease risk 3-4 fold and favors ileal over colonic involvement.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick identifies smoking as a modifiable lifestyle risk factor for autoimmune disease and states in its clinical correlation that the risk of developing Crohn's disease is 3-4 times higher in smokers than non-smokers, and that ileal involvement is more likely than colonic involvement in smokers.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Smoking does change risk; it raises it 3-4 fold.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Smoking increases rather than decreases risk, and it favors ileal rather than colonic disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The 20-40 fold figure applies to carrying two mutated NOD2 alleles, not smoking, and smokers have more ileal, not colonic, involvement.
whyWrongByChoice.D: The magnitude is correct, but smokers are more likely to have ileal, not colonic, involvement.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy has recurrent episodes of fever accompanied by abdominal pain, a maculopapular rash, and mouth ulcers. His parents are unaffected. Laboratory evaluation during attacks shows increased inflammasome activity with overexpression of IL-1, and no autoantibodies are detected. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acute rheumatic fever

choices.label: B
choices.text: Crohn's disease

choices.label: C
choices.text: Familial Mediterranean fever

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mevalonate kinase deficiency

choices.label: E
choices.text: Systemic lupus erythematosus

explanation.summary: Mevalonate kinase deficiency is an autosomal recessive pyrin loss-of-function autoinflammatory disease presenting with fever, abdominal pain, maculopapular rash, and ulcers.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick names two monogenic autosomal recessive autoinflammatory diseases resulting from pyrin loss-of-function: familial Mediterranean fever and mevalonate kinase deficiency (MKD), both with increased inflammasome activity and IL-1 overexpression. It lists the symptoms of MKD as fever, abdominal pain, maculopapular rash, and ulcers, matching this child. Unaffected parents are consistent with recessive inheritance.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Acute rheumatic fever follows streptococcal infection and is antibody-mediated via molecular mimicry, not an inflammasome disorder.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Crohn's disease is a complex autoinflammatory IBD with chronic diarrhea and weight loss linked to NOD2 mutations, not a periodic fever syndrome with IL-1 overexpression from pyrin loss.
whyWrongByChoice.C: FMF shares the mechanism, but its symptoms are fever, peritonitis, an erysipelas-like rash, and arthritis of a single joint, not a maculopapular rash with ulcers.
whyWrongByChoice.E: SLE is an autoimmune type 3 hypersensitivity with autoantibodies; this child has none.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A geneticist investigates a family with a rare hereditary syndrome of recurrent fevers and neutrophilic tissue inflammation. Affected members have no autoantibodies. Which of the following molecular defects is consistent with an autoinflammatory etiology?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Accumulation of misfolded proteins that promotes inflammatory cytokine secretion

choices.label: B
choices.text: An HLA allele that increases TCR affinity for a self-peptide

choices.label: C
choices.text: Antibodies that cross-react with a self-protein resembling a microbial antigen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Failure of negative selection of self-reactive thymocytes

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced apoptosis of autoreactive lymphocytes under high estrogen levels

explanation.summary: Autoinflammatory etiologies include mutated inflammasomes, insufficient clearance of inflammation-associated proteins, inability to regulate cytokine signaling, and accumulation of misfolded proteins that promotes cytokine secretion.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that autoinflammatory diseases are due to dysregulation of the innate immune system resulting in unchecked inflammatory cytokines or activation of innate immune cells, and lists the etiologies as mutated inflammasomes, insufficient clearance of inflammation-associated proteins, inability to regulate cytokine signaling, or accumulation of misfolded proteins that promotes secretion of inflammatory cytokines. Only choice A belongs to this list.

whyWrongByChoice.B: HLA risk alleles that increase TCR affinity for self-antigen are an intrinsic genetic mechanism of autoimmunity, not autoinflammation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Cross-reactive antibodies describe molecular mimicry, an infection-triggered autoimmune mechanism; the family has no autoantibodies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Failure of negative selection is a breakdown of central tolerance, an autoimmune mechanism; autoinflammatory diseases do not involve tolerance breakdown.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Estrogen-related persistence of autoreactive lymphocytes is the brick's postulated explanation for female predominance of autoimmune disease.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman with two episodes of transient visual loss and limb weakness separated by several months is diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. Which of the following genetic findings is associated with her disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A CTLA-4 allele that lowers CTLA-4 expression on regulatory T cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: A NOD2 mutation that causes inappropriate NF-kB activation in intestinal cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: A pyrin mutation that removes inflammasome suppression in neutrophils

choices.label: D
choices.text: A TNF-alpha receptor variant that is secreted rather than membrane-bound

choices.label: E
choices.text: The HLA-DR4 allele associated with rheumatoid arthritis and type 1 diabetes

explanation.summary: A variant in the TNF-alpha receptor gene that causes the receptor to be secreted instead of membrane-bound is associated with multiple sclerosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Under intrinsic factors, the brick gives two examples of diverse genetic influences: an allele affecting CTLA-4 expression that increases risk of celiac disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and SLE, and a variant in the gene for a TNF-alpha receptor that causes it to be secreted (versus membrane-bound), which is associated with multiple sclerosis. Multiple sclerosis is also listed with HLA-DR2 in Table 1.

whyWrongByChoice.A: The CTLA-4 allele is linked to celiac disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and SLE, not multiple sclerosis.
whyWrongByChoice.B: NOD2 mutations are the strongest risk factor for Crohn's disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Pyrin loss-of-function causes the autoinflammatory diseases FMF and mevalonate kinase deficiency.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HLA-DR4 is associated with rheumatoid arthritis, type 1 diabetes, and Addison disease; multiple sclerosis is associated with HLA-DR2.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: HLA genes encode MHC class I and class II proteins that present antigen for T-cell development and activation. Which of the following correctly pairs an MHC class with its cellular distribution and function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: MHC class I; antigen-presenting cells only; presentation of antigen to cytotoxic T cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: MHC class I; antigen-presenting cells only; presentation of antigen to helper T cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: MHC class I; every nucleated cell; recognition of infected or malignant cells by cytotoxic T cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: MHC class II; antigen-presenting cells only; recognition of infected cells by cytotoxic T cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: MHC class II; every nucleated cell; recognition of infected or malignant cells by cytotoxic T cells

explanation.summary: MHC class I is expressed on every nucleated cell and functions in cytotoxic T-cell recognition of abnormal cells; MHC class II is on antigen-presenting cells and presents antigen to helper T cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick recalls that MHC class I molecules are expressed on every nucleated cell in the body and function in cytotoxic T cell (CTL) recognition of abnormal (infected or malignant) cells, whereas MHC class II gene products are present on antigen-presenting cells, which present antigen to helper T cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: MHC class I is expressed on every nucleated cell, not only on antigen-presenting cells.
whyWrongByChoice.B: MHC class I is on every nucleated cell, not restricted to APCs, and it serves cytotoxic rather than helper T cells.
whyWrongByChoice.D: MHC class II presents antigen to helper T cells, not cytotoxic T cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MHC class II is restricted to antigen-presenting cells, not every nucleated cell.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: Structural studies of a risk-associated HLA-DR molecule show that specific amino acids at positions 13 and 71 of the HLA-DR beta chain allow the CDR3 region of a T-cell receptor to interact best with a bound self-antigen. This finding best illustrates which of the following mechanisms by which HLA risk alleles promote autoimmunity?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Epitope spreading to additional self-antigens

choices.label: B
choices.text: Escape of self-reactive T cells from negative selection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased T-cell receptor affinity for the self-antigen

choices.label: D
choices.text: Molecular mimicry between viral and self peptides

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reduced apoptosis of autoreactive lymphocytes

explanation.summary: HLA risk alleles can promote autoimmunity by increasing TCR affinity for a self-antigen, as illustrated by HLA-DR residues 13 and 71 shaping the CDR3 interaction.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick asks why specific HLA alleles convey risk and gives two answers: HLA risk alleles may influence central tolerance so that self-reactive T cells are more likely to pass and be released, and they may increase TCR affinity for the self-antigen. Figure 3 provides the example of an HLA-DR whose amino acids at positions 13 and 71 determine how well the TCR CDR3 region interacts with the bound antigen, illustrating the affinity mechanism.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Epitope spreading is an amplification loop that broadens an established response; it does not describe HLA-peptide-TCR binding.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Influence on central tolerance is the brick's other HLA mechanism, but the finding described is about strength of TCR binding to the presented peptide, not thymic selection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Molecular mimicry involves homology between microbial and self antigens and is an environmental (infection) trigger, not an HLA structural effect.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Reduced apoptosis of autoreactive lymphocytes is the postulated estrogen-related mechanism for female predominance.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: Two sisters are evaluated for celiac disease risk. One is homozygous for HLA-DQ2 and the other carries a single HLA-DQ2 allele. Which of the following best describes their relative risk of developing celiac disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Both have equal risk, because a single DQ2 allele confers maximal risk

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both have equal risk, because HLA-DQ8 rather than DQ2 determines susceptibility

choices.label: C
choices.text: Neither is at increased risk, because celiac disease is associated with HLA-DR4

choices.label: D
choices.text: The heterozygous sister has the higher risk, because homozygosity is protective

choices.label: E
choices.text: The homozygous sister has the higher risk, because the HLA-DQ2 effect is dose-dependent

explanation.summary: The influence of celiac-associated HLA alleles is dose-dependent, and homozygosity carries the most risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick's clinical correlation states that almost 95% of patients with celiac disease express HLA-DQ2 (the rest usually carry HLA-DQ8), that the influence of these HLA alleles is dose-dependent, and that homozygosity carries the most risk of developing celiac disease. Gluten epitopes bind with higher stability to DQ2 molecules than to other MHC alleles, hypothesized to reflect the specific amino acids holding the peptide in the peptide-binding groove via non-covalent bonding.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Risk is dose-dependent, so two DQ2 alleles confer more risk than one.
whyWrongByChoice.B: DQ2 is present in almost 95% of celiac patients; DQ8 accounts for most of the remainder, and the dose effect applies to these alleles.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Celiac disease is associated with HLA-DQ2/DQ8; HLA-DR4 is linked to rheumatoid arthritis, type 1 diabetes, and Addison disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Homozygosity increases, not decreases, risk.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A 40-year-old patient with a strong family history of autoimmune disease asks which risk factors could be changed. Which of the following is a modifiable environmental risk factor for autoimmune disease?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A CTLA-4 risk allele

choices.label: B
choices.text: Being of child-bearing age

choices.label: C
choices.text: Carrying the HLA-DR4 allele

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cigarette smoking

choices.label: E
choices.text: Female sex

explanation.summary: Modifiable risk factors are environmental factors such as smoking, extreme temperatures, and occupational exposures.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick divides autoimmune risk into intrinsic factors (genetics, hormones), environmental factors, and amplification loops. Environmental factors include modifiable risk factors and infections; modifiable risk factors include lifestyle choices such as smoking and hazards of living and working environments such as extreme temperatures and occupational exposures.

whyWrongByChoice.A: A CTLA-4 allele is an intrinsic genetic influence, not an environmental exposure.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Age is an intrinsic factor that cannot be modified.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HLA alleles are intrinsic genetic factors and cannot be modified.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Sex is an intrinsic factor; most autoimmune diseases are more common in women.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: During an acute viral infection of the liver, virus-specific CD8+ T cells release perforin and granzymes that kill infected hepatocytes. Nearby uninfected hepatocytes also die, and the inflammatory milieu activates other immune cells within the tissue. This process is best described as which of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Bystander activation

choices.label: B
choices.text: Epitope spreading

choices.label: C
choices.text: Molecular mimicry

choices.label: D
choices.text: Negative selection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Receptor editing

explanation.summary: Bystander activation is infection-driven collateral killing of uninfected cells by CTL granules with activation of surrounding cells by the inflammatory milieu.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick describes bystander activation (Figure 4, right): infected cells present viral antigens to virus-specific CTLs, which release cytotoxic granules, causing death of infected cells as well as nearby uninfected cells, and the inflammatory milieu leads to activation of bystander cells within the tissue. Infections can trigger or exacerbate autoimmunity through this bystander effect.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Epitope spreading is the expansion of the immune response to additional epitopes revealed by tissue damage, a downstream amplification phenomenon rather than the direct collateral killing described.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Molecular mimicry requires a receptor that recognizes both a viral antigen and a homologous self-antigen; the stem describes collateral damage, not cross-reactivity.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Negative selection deletes self-reactive developing lymphocytes and is unrelated to CTL killing in infected tissue.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Receptor editing is a central tolerance process in developing B cells in the bone marrow.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: An immunologist studying a virus-triggered autoimmune reaction wants to determine whether it arose from molecular mimicry rather than bystander activation. Which of the following findings would specifically support molecular mimicry?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cytokines in the inflamed tissue activate lymphocytes that are not virus-specific

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cytotoxic granules from virus-specific CTLs kill adjacent uninfected cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Damaged cells leak hidden self-antigens that APCs present to autoreactive T cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Infected cells present viral antigen to virus-specific cytotoxic T cells

choices.label: E
choices.text: One T-cell receptor reacts to a viral antigen and a homologous self-antigen

explanation.summary: Molecular mimicry is defined by a receptor recognizing both a microbial antigen and a self-antigen that share structural or sequential homology.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that in molecular mimicry (Figure 4, left), TCRs recognize and react toward both viral antigens and self-antigens that have structural or sequential homology. A single TCR cross-reacting with a viral antigen and a homologous self-antigen is the defining feature that distinguishes mimicry from bystander activation, in which autoreactivity arises from collateral damage and the inflammatory milieu rather than shared antigen structure.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Activation of non-virus-specific cells by the inflammatory milieu is part of bystander activation, not mimicry.
whyWrongByChoice.B: Killing of adjacent uninfected cells by CTL granules is the hallmark of bystander activation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Leakage of hidden self-antigens with subsequent presentation to autoreactive T cells describes epitope spreading.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Presentation of viral antigen to virus-specific CTLs is the normal antiviral response that initiates bystander activation and does not demonstrate cross-reactivity.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is diagnosed with Goodpasture syndrome. Which of the following HLA subtypes is most associated with his condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: HLA-DQ2

choices.label: B
choices.text: HLA-DR2

choices.label: C
choices.text: HLA-DR4

choices.label: D
choices.text: HLA-DQ8

choices.label: E
choices.text: HLA-B27

explanation.summary: HLA-DR2 is associated with multiple sclerosis, SLE, and Goodpasture syndrome.
explanation.whyCorrect: Table 1 of the brick lists the HLA subtypes and associated diseases that need to be known: DR2 is paired with multiple sclerosis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and Goodpasture syndrome. The brick stresses that virtually all autoimmune diseases are associated with specific HLA genes.

whyWrongByChoice.A: HLA-DQ2 is associated with celiac disease.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HLA-DR4 is associated with rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes mellitus type 1, and Addison disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: HLA-DQ8 is associated with celiac disease.
whyWrongByChoice.E: HLA-B27 is associated with psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, IBD-associated arthritis, and reactive arthritis.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: During a viral infection, cytotoxic T lymphocytes kill infected cells. Days later, antigen-presenting cells begin presenting self-antigens to autoreactive T cells, which then attack uninfected cells carrying those antigens. Which of the following events most directly made these self-antigens available for presentation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Affinity maturation of virus-specific B cells

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cross-reaction of one TCR with viral and self peptides

choices.label: C
choices.text: Escape of self-reactive T cells from thymic deletion

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leakage of hidden self-antigens from cells killed by CTLs

choices.label: E
choices.text: Release of cytokines by helper T cells early in infection

explanation.summary: In epitope spreading, CTL-mediated apoptosis lets hidden self-antigens leak from damaged cells, which APCs then present to autoreactive T cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Figure 5 of the brick lays out epitope spreading: steps 1-4 are a classic viral response, in step 5 CTL-mediated apoptosis allows hidden self-antigens to leak from damaged cells, in step 6 APCs present these self-antigens to autoreactive T cells, and in step 7 those T cells attack normal cells carrying the self-antigens. The brick summarizes this as the viral response revealing hidden self-antigens that activate self-reactive T cells.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Affinity maturation of B cells refines antibody responses and is not what exposes intracellular self-antigens.
whyWrongByChoice.B: TCR cross-reactivity with homologous viral and self peptides is molecular mimicry, which does not require release of hidden antigens.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Escape from negative selection explains why autoreactive T cells exist, not how previously hidden antigens became available to APCs.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Helper T-cell cytokine release (step 3) is part of the classic antiviral response and does not itself expose hidden self-antigens.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: In a patient with long-standing systemic lupus erythematosus, autoreactive B cells produce antibodies of progressively higher affinity through affinity maturation and somatic hypermutation. Immune complexes of autoantibody and self-antigen drive this refinement through presentation by which of the following cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cytotoxic CD8+ T lymphocytes

choices.label: B
choices.text: Follicular dendritic cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: Long-lived plasma cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Neutrophils in the follicle

choices.label: E
choices.text: Regulatory T cells (FOXP3+)

explanation.summary: Immune complexes of antibody and self-antigen promote affinity maturation of autoreactive B cells via presentation by follicular dendritic cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: Among the brick's examples of epitope spreading in autoimmunity, it states that over time the repertoire of autoreactive B cells is refined by affinity maturation and somatic hypermutation, and that immune complexes of antibody and self-antigen promote affinity maturation via presentation by follicular dendritic cells. SLE is one of the diseases in which epitope spreading has been observed.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes kill infected cells and, in epitope spreading, release hidden self-antigens; they do not drive B-cell affinity maturation.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Plasma cells secrete antibody; they are a product of B-cell maturation rather than the cells presenting immune complexes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Neutrophils are innate effector cells responsible for autoinflammatory tissue damage, not immune-complex presentation to B cells.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Regulatory T cells suppress excessive immune activation and maintain tolerance; they do not present immune complexes to B cells.

questions.topicName: Introduction to Autoinflammatory and Autoimmune Diseases

questions.stem: A patient has a chronic autoimmune disease in which regulatory T-cell activity is impaired. Which of the following best explains how this impairment sustains chronic inflammation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Autoreactive B cells undergo receptor editing

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inflammasome activity increases and IL-1 is overproduced

choices.label: C
choices.text: MHC class II expression is lost from antigen-presenting cells

choices.label: D
choices.text: Negative selection in the thymus becomes more stringent

choices.label: E
choices.text: Unchecked T-cell responses expand epitope recognition

explanation.summary: When regulatory T-cell activity is impaired, unchecked T-cell responses lead to expanding epitope recognition, fueling chronic inflammation.
explanation.whyCorrect: The brick states that regulatory T cells ordinarily suppress excessive immune activation and maintain tolerance, and that in diseases where Treg activity is impaired, unchecked T-cell responses lead to expanding epitope recognition, fueling chronic inflammation. This is one of the amplification loops that prolongs or exacerbates autoimmune damage.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Receptor editing is a bone marrow central tolerance process for developing B cells and is not triggered by loss of Treg activity.
whyWrongByChoice.B: IL-1 overproduction from excess inflammasome activity is the innate mechanism of autoinflammatory disease, not a consequence of Treg impairment.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Loss of MHC class II would reduce antigen presentation to helper T cells; the brick describes enhanced, not reduced, presentation during amplification.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Treg impairment affects peripheral suppression; it does not make thymic negative selection more stringent, and stricter selection would reduce, not sustain, autoimmunity.
